topic: Human bioluminescence: ultraweak light emitted by the body
hook: Your body glows in the dark
caption:
Right now, your body is giving off visible light. In 2009, researchers in Japan used ultra-sensitive cameras in total darkness and filmed people glowing, mostly from the face and neck.

The light is about 1,000 times too weak for your eyes. It rises and falls during the day and peaks in the late afternoon. Source: Kobayashi et al., PLoS ONE (2009).

Follow for one body fact your brain won't believe, every day. Did you know humans glow, or is this new to you?

1/4 Your body glows in the dark
A 2009 Japanese study filmed people in total darkness and caught faint visible light coming from their skin.
🎨 AI-generated image

2/4 Too faint to see (1000x)
The glow is about 1,000 times weaker than what human eyes can detect. Only ultra-sensitive cameras saw it.
📷 DOE/FNAL/DECam/R. Hahn/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

3/4 Made by your cells
Chemical reactions involving free radicals in your metabolism release tiny bursts of light particles called photons.
🎨 AI-generated image

4/4 Brightest at 4 PM (4 PM)
Your glow follows a daily rhythm: dimmest around 10 a.m., brightest around 4 p.m. Your cheeks shine the most.
